title: Tseitin encoding characterizes gate evaluation
statement: Let $g$ be a gate with at most two inputs, let $z$ be a natural-number index, and let $a$ assign a Boolean value to every natural-number index. For a Boolean value list $v$, suppose the value of $v$ at each input index of $g$, with out-of-range indices treated as false, equals the value assigned there by $a$. Then the Tseitin encoding of $g$ at $z$ is satisfied by $a$ if and only if the value assigned to $z$ equals the evaluation of $g$ on $v$.
hypotheses_covered: The gate has at most two inputs
An assignment of Boolean values to natural-number indices
